intro: Leaning into the steep side of the Maçka valley, in Trabzon province, stands Vazelon Monastery, a monastery and church founded in 270. It is older than Sümela, and under the Empire of Trebizond it kept the land registers of the region.
history: The monastery was founded in 270, about a century before Sümela. Set into the steep side of the Maçka valley, it kept the land and tax registers of the region under the Empire of Trebizond. Those records are among the most important sources for the medieval social history of the Black Sea. In 1923 the monastery was abandoned.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the main church, the frescoes, the monks' cells and the rock-cut stairs.
facts: Did you know? The Vazelon Registers list villagers by name, with their shares of land. That makes them one of the rare medieval documents in which ordinary people are named at all. And the monastery was founded in 270, about a century before Sümela.
outro: This brings our tour of Vazelon Monastery to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
